title: The AC/AT model cannot express partial coverage, so a half-covered criterion gates green
body:
The AC/AT model cannot express PARTIAL coverage: `covers` is a whole-criterion edge, so an AT that genuinely asserts half of an AC either reads as covering all of it (a green gate over an unverified half) or the estate invents a local convention to say otherwise.

**The failing shape, live on Conflab (2026-08-28):** AC-02.4's panel-survival half is unobservable by unit test; the covering AT asserts the other half; `ac gate` read the thread as PASSING both gates while the unverified half sat invisible -- the gate was not wrong but BLIND, and the shape is undetectable by the gate BY CONSTRUCTION (conflab-vc). The two instances were closed by hv's fiat with the half recorded ACCEPTED UNVERIFIED (Conflab `39ad847c`); the closes repaired the instances and did not touch the class. Per conflab-vc: these two are unlikely to be the only instances.

**Intent's own estate carries the workaround for the same inexpressibility, which is how we know the gap is real in both directions:** ST0056's AT-00.6 is held `red` explicitly FOR partial coverage ("AC-00.8 IS A FIVE-CLAUSE ROLL-UP AND THIS FILE ASSERTS ONE CLAUSE"), with the convention documented in the row note and enforced by nothing. So one estate under-reports (green over a half) and this one over-reports (red on a file whose own tests pass), and both are the model saying the true state has no field.

**Fix direction, not prescribed:** make partial coverage expressible -- per-clause coverage, a qualifier on the `covers` edge, or a first-class partial state -- so the gate can see it and neither estate needs a convention. Related: ST0066 (fiat close) exists partly because unverifiable halves need a legitimate authority-based exit; this issue is the other side -- making the half VISIBLE so the exit is a choice rather than a blind green.
